text.tspan: When the world is actually out to get you,
always assume someone will try to break your stuff.
always check that functions you call succeed.
always assume your code will have problems.
try to make problems easy to detect and address.
Assume the stupidity of all parties:
the user won’t read the documentation (neither will the dev)
error codes should have unambiguous, detailed explanations
don’t expect files to stay the same across calss unless you
never return pointers or indices into arrays
Things are not impossible. Just highly
Decide how to deal with impossible cases.
using assert statements to constrain values and fail fast
intentionally crashing in unsafe conditions (i.e. Rust
the actual array of queue elements
head index in que of the queue
max number of elements in queue
